title: James: faith that works

lines: James reads less like an argument than a string of sharp, practical sayings from a pastor who has watched faith go soft.
The church has long held that its writer was the brother of Jesus, who once did not believe and became a leader in Jerusalem.

scripture.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ

lines: Look for threads rather than a tidy outline: trials, wisdom, wealth, speech, faith and deeds, taken up again and again from new angles.
It sounds like Proverbs, and still more like the Sermon on the Mount.
Be doers of the word, and not hearers only.

scripture.text: Be doers of the word, and not hearers only.

lines: James opens by calling trials an occasion for joy. Not because suffering is good, but because tested faith produces perseverance, and perseverance leads to maturity.
He's honest that trials hurt, and he insists that God tempts no one and gives only good gifts.

scripture.text: the testing of your faith develops perseverance.

lines: Faith that does nothing is dead. It's the faith of bare words, which tells the hungry to keep warm and gives nothing.
So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.

Paul and James both teach that God saves by grace and that true faith is alive. They use faith, works, and justify in different senses. Christians relate the two in several ways, and this film takes no side.

scripture.text: So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.

lines: Few books speak so sharply about wealth. James condemns giving the best seats to the rich, warns the rich that they fade like a flower, and pronounces woe on those who hold back wages.

scripture.text: Has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith

lines: Every chapter touches the tongue. A small spark sets a great forest ablaze. Speech is the clearest test of whether faith has reached the whole person.
Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger.

scripture.text: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger

lines: Read all five chapters at one sitting. It takes about fifteen minutes. Watch the threads, and read it beside the Sermon on the Mount.
The key chapters are one, two, three, and five.

scripture.text: he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault

lines: James wants a faith that works.
